lines: """Run asynchronous jobs with bounded concurrency and orderly cancellation."""
"""Run jobs, waiting for their cleanup before returning or raising.
Jobs are started in list order, with at most ``max_concurrent`` running.
If a job fails or the caller is cancelled, running jobs are cancelled and
awaited; jobs that have not started are skipped. The original exception
propagates after cleanup. With ``asyncio.run``, this also handles the first
Ctrl-C, which cancels the main coroutine.
Jobs should release resources in ``finally`` blocks and cooperate with
cancellation. ``max_concurrent`` must be a positive integer.
raise TypeError("max_concurrent must be an integer")
raise ValueError("max_concurrent must be greater than zero")
# Shield the workers so cancellation is delivered only once below;
# cancelling them twice could interrupt their asynchronous cleanup.
# The shield may have been cancelled before it could retrieve this
# future's exception. All workers have now finished, so it is ready.
